title: Annotating Slack Directly on Your Verilog: Fine-Grained RTL Timing Evaluation for Early Optimization
problem: Timing information is typically unavailable at the early RTL stage of IC design, and while ML solutions can predict design-level TNS/WNS metrics, fine-grained timing information for individual registers remains unavailable. This limits register-level timing optimization at the stage where design flexibility is greatest.
motivation: The early RTL stage offers greater optimization flexibility than post-synthesis or layout stages, making fine-grained timing visibility at this stage critical for enabling better design optimization.
method: RTL-Timer trains a machine learning model on multiple structural representations of chip designs to predict timing slack (available buffer time) for individual registers. The model uses specialized training objectives designed to capture the latest moment signals can arrive at each register endpoint without exceeding the timing deadline. These predictions then guide standard chip design tools to optimize the circuit in register-aware ways, enabling timing optimization at the early code stage when designs are most flexible to change.
key_novelty: RTL-Timer is the first to predict per-register timing slack (available buffer time before timing failures) at the code design stage, making fine-grained timing optimization possible where design changes are cheapest.
contributions: RTL-Timer, the first fine-grained RTL timing predictor applicable to any design
Multiple RTL representation approaches for capturing timing information
Customized loss functions to accurately model maximum arrival time at register endpoints
Demonstration of 3% WNS and 10% TNS improvement when guiding synthesis optimization with RTL-Timer predictions
primary_theme: ML-based register-level timing prediction for RTL optimization
